learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: Linear Algebra, geometry, differential geometry, differential and integral calculus, differential and partial differential equations, numerical methods and numerical algorithms.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to know, understand and use the basic principles of Linear Algebra.

syllabus_topics: Linear dependence and independence. Bases. Coordinates. Dimension.
Vector subspaces. Direct sum. Complementary subspaces.
The matrix of a linear map. Change of base.
Diagonalization of endomorphisms and matrices. Matrix similarity.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, progressive evaluation is applied through two individual written tests: the first with 30% weight and the second with 70% weight. Students pass if the weighted average is 5 out of 10 points or more. Students who do not pass the progressive evaluation may take a single global exam covering the entire syllabus, where the final grade will be that obtained in this exam, requiring 5 or more to pass. For the extraordinary call, evaluation is done through a final exam, also requiring 5 or more to pass. A 'No Show' grade is given if a student does not attend any of the tests.
